verses.text: Here are more of Solomon's proverbs. The men who served Hezekiah, king of Judah, copied them down.
God's glory is in keeping a thing hidden. The glory of kings is in searching a matter out.
The heavens stretch high and the earth goes deep. The hearts of kings are just as hard to fathom.
Skim the waste off the silver, and the refiner has something to work with.
Remove wicked people from the king's presence, and his throne will stand firm on what's right.
Don't hype yourself up in front of the king or claim a spot among important people.
It's better to hear, “Come up here,” than to get sent down to a lower seat in front of the prince you came to see.
Don't rush to drag your neighbor into court. What'll you do when they embarrass you in the end?
Talk through the dispute with your neighbor. Keep what someone else told you in confidence to yourself.
Otherwise whoever hears it could shame you, and that bad name could stick with you for good.
The right word at the right moment is like golden apples set in silver.
Wise correction to someone willing to listen is like a gold earring or jewelry made of fine gold.
A reliable messenger feels like snow-cold refreshment at harvest to the people who sent them. They revive their masters' spirits.
Someone who brags about gifts they never give is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
Patience can persuade a ruler. Gentle words can break a bone.
Found some honey? Eat just enough. Too much and you'll throw it back up.
Don't show up at your neighbor's place all the time. They might get tired of you and end up hating you.
Lying about your neighbor in court hits like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Depending on somebody who breaks trust when trouble hits is like trying to chew with a bad tooth or walk on an injured foot.
Singing songs to someone with a heavy heart is like taking their coat when it's cold or pouring vinegar on soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give them something to eat. If they're thirsty, give them water.
Doing that heaps burning coals on their head, and the LORD will reward you.
The north wind brings rain, and talking behind people's backs brings angry faces.
Better to live in a corner up on the roof than share a house with a woman who's always picking fights.
Good news from far away feels like cold water when you're dying of thirst.
A person who does right but caves in to the wicked is like a muddy spring or a polluted well.
Too much honey isn't good for you. Chasing your own honor doesn't bring you honor either.
A person with no self-control is like a wrecked city with no walls.
